title: helm(private): values schema + init hooks to support terraform-managed secrets and robust upgrade/rollback
author: Ethan Kim
body: Motivation: Private installer customers who manage secrets via Terraform (KMS-wrapped secrets, external secret stores, or platform-level secret managers) need a predictable Helm chart that can accept externally provisioned secrets, validate values, and handle upgrades/rollbacks without leaving init jobs or CRDs in a broken state. This PR extends the redwood-private Helm chart with a more expressive values.schema.json, templating knobs for terraform-managed secret references, safer init and upgrade hooks, and clearer upgrade/rollback guidance. What changed: 1) values.schema.json: added terraformSecretRef and externalSecret references for components that require credentials (api, console, operator). Schema includes oneOf to allow either inline credentials or a secretRef object, with descriptive validation messages to aid CI. 2) Templates: added templates/init-terraform-secrets.yaml (pre-install) and templates/upgrade-rollback-hook.yaml (pre-upgrade/post-upgrade) that detect terraformSecretRef and annotate jobs to be non-blocking when appropriate (helm.sh/hook-weight, delete-policies). Hooks are idempotent and include TTLSecondsAfterFinished to avoid orphaned Jobs. 3) Templating helpers: _helpers.tpl now exposes tpl-safe functions for secretRef resolution and a new chart helper `redwood.fullSecretName` to maintain stable secret names across upgrades. 4) CRD handling: added post-install crd-verify job to ensure CRDs are applied before controller rollouts; compatible with earlier CRD upgrade hooks. 5) Docs and examples: docs/upgrade.md updated with explicit rollback instructions when using terraform-managed secrets; examples/terraform/README.md shows recommended flow for applying secrets out-of-band and using helm upgrade --wait with adjusted timeout. 6) Tests: added chart tests/values-validate.yaml and CI helm unit tests to validate schema and common templating paths. Backwards compatibility: schema changes are additive; charts that still use inline secrets continue to work. For clusters that already rely on legacy init hooks, new hooks include compatibility annotations to skip when legacy job markers exist. Migration notes: when migrating to terraformSecretRef, create the external secret in the cluster prior to running helm upgrade. The pre-install hook will no-op if the referenced Secret exists. Testing: local helm lint + schema validation, CI runs helm unit tests and the chart acceptance suite against kind clusters; manual validation done on a staging VPC deployment. Security considerations: templates avoid printing secret values to logs; jobs mount secrets with read-only permissions; KMS/HSM integrations still handled out-of-band by Terraform and external secret controllers. Release notes: see release_notes field. Rollout plan: merge to main, include chart bump to v2.8.0, ship as part of private-installer 2026.02 release. Contact: @ethan for follow-ups and rollouts.

Miguel Alvarez: How does this interact with KMS-wrapped values or external secret operators? We should explicitly state expectations.
Ethan Kim: Updated docs to call out KMS/HSM expectations and that Terraform or an external secret controller must populate the Secret object prior to helm upgrade.
Ava Martinez: Minor templating nits (helpers naming). Approving after rebase and a small rename in _helpers.tpl to avoid collision with existing helper names.

release_notes: Helm chart (redwood-private) v2.8.0: Added support for terraform-managed secrets via values.schema.json (terraformSecretRef/externalSecret), new idempotent pre-install and upgrade hooks to safely handle out-of-band secrets, improved CRD verification job to avoid controller rollouts before CRDs are present, docs and examples for migrating from inline secrets to external secret workflows; no breaking changes.
summary: Adds schema-level support for terraform-managed secrets, safer init/upgrade hooks, CRD verification, docs/examples and CI acceptance tests to the redwood-private Helm chart to improve Private installer reliability when secrets are managed out-of-band by Terraform or external secret controllers.
